sentences.text: The applicants are lodged in jail since 17/08/2023 and 03/03/2025 respectively.

The first bail application of applicant Shravan was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to renew prayer after examination of prosecutrix and eye witness of the incident before the trial Court, and second application M.Cr.C. No.49062/2023 was dismissed for want of prosecution.

4. Counsel for the applicants have submitted that the examination-in- chief of the prosecutrix has been recorded on 26/09/2024, however, subsequently she failed to appear in the trial Court on as many as 7 occasions.
It is also submitted that in her examination-in-chief, it is mentioned by the prosecutrix that Shyam Singh was driving the vehicle and Shravan was also present on the spot.

Counsel has also drawn the attention of this Court to the statement of one independent witness namely Kishor Das, who has also stated that the prosecutrix, who had come to his house along with co-accused Shyam Singh was happy and was also wearing Sindoor, and did not inform about her abduction.

Thus, it is submitted that the bail applications be allowed and applicants be released on bail as they are lodged in jail since 17/08/2023 and 03/03/2025 and conclusion of trial is likely to take time.

5. Counsel for the respondent / State, on the other hand has opposed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:17046 3 MCRC-19899-2025 the prayer and it is submitted that no case for grant of bail is made out, however, it is not denied that the names of the present applicants have not been mentioned in the FIR.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and on perusal of the case diary as also the earlier order passed by this Court, taking note of the fact that the prosecutrix is not appearing in the trial Court since last 7 occasions, and the applicants are lodged in jail since 17/08/2023 and 03/03/2025 respectively, this Court finds force in the submissions as advanced by the counsel for the applicant,
and is of the considered opinion that the applicants' applications deserve to be allowed.
7.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the applications filed by the applicants are allowed.

The applicants are directed to be released on bail upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (rupees twenty five thousand) each with one solvent surety each of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for their regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that they shall remain present before the court concerned during trial and shall also abide by the conditions enumerated under Section 437 (3) Criminal Procedure Code, 1973.
8. M.Cr.C. stands allowed.
